Definition: from a derivative of G5188; to envelop with smoke, i.e. (figuratively) to inflate with self-conceit:--high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud.
BiblicalUsage: typhóō is the word for to puff up, to inflate with pride. In 1 Timothy 3:6, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil, and it appears again in 1 Timothy 6:4. In the Greek text the word is spelled τυφόομαι.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe typhóō still tells the truth about God, and I take it as it stands.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
